def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Output-boundary predication: compress the wide tile-overhang penalty.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[9]
    # Final-wave underfill leaves SMs idle after the preceding waves finish.
    s = s + f.tail_waste * w[18]
    # A small grid does not amortize CTA dispatch and wave startup overhead.
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[7]
    # Any register spill introduces a qualitatively slower local-memory path.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[17]
    # Spill severity captures the resulting local-memory traffic beyond the binary event.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[10]
    # Pipeline prologue and epilogue are exposed when the K loop is short.
    s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[6]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        # In a memory-bound GEMM, replicated operand loads directly increase bandwidth demand.
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[8]
        # Low-intensity CTA tiles make each fetched operand support little arithmetic.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[4]
        if p.log_min_dim < 6 or p.log_flops < 35:
            # Short or skinny reductions cannot amortize multistage buffering and synchronization.
            s = s + f.pipeline_family * w[19]
        else:
            # Long reductions amortize the structural family cost over a steady-state pipeline.
            s = s + f.pipeline_family * w[20]
    else:
        # In a compute-bound GEMM, excessive instruction work competes with tensor issue capacity.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[0]
        # Compute-bound throughput is reduced when thread and CTA resources hide less latency.
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[12]
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[14]
        if p.log_min_dim < 6 or p.log_flops < 35:
            # Resource-limited compute kernels expose family synchronization and buffer overhead.
            s = s + f.pipeline_family * w[19]
        else:
            # For long compute loops, only the smaller steady-state family penalty remains.
            s = s + f.pipeline_family * w[20]
    # Square-like outputs retain a mismatch penalty; rectangular outputs can favor
    # squarer CTAs when improved grid and wave filling outweigh nominal mismatch.
    s = s + np.where(p.output_aspect_imbalance < 0.5,
                     f.tile_aspect_mismatch * w[3],
                     f.tile_aspect_mismatch * w[2])
    # Shared-layout padding distinguishes swizzle choices with similar tile and pipeline shapes.
    s = s + f.shared_access_padding_fraction * w[11]
    # Excess shared-memory allocation reduces residency and buffering headroom.
    s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[1]
    if p.log_flops >= 33.2131 and p.output_work_per_sm < 234057:
        # split-K sweet spot: quadratic in log2(K-loop iterations per serial split), interior optimum
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count)) * w[16]
        s = s + np.square(np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count))) * w[13]
    if p.roofline_ratio >= 1 and p.output_work_per_sm > 200000:
        # large-grid branch (r09): CTA residency and register pressure on huge compute-bound grids
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[5] + f.register_file_pressure * w[15]
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Output-tile overhang: compress the wide edge-waste range.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[21]
    # Any register spill introduces exceptionally expensive local-memory accesses.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[7]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[28]
    # A nearly empty final wave leaves a rapidly growing fraction of the GPU idle.
    s = s + (-np.log2(np.maximum(1.0e-6, 1.0 - f.tail_waste))) * w[5]
    # Small grids expose launch and CTA-dispatch startup overhead.
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[1]
    # Pipeline prologue/epilogue cost is poorly amortized by short reductions.
    s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[0]
    s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[27]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1.0:
        # In the bandwidth-bound regime, replicated operand loads dominate.
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[19]
        # Low-intensity CTA tiles directly increase bandwidth pressure.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[8]
        # Parallel split-K partials add global-memory traffic in this regime.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[9]
    else:
        # In the compute-bound regime, front-end instruction overhead is exposed.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[4]
        # Thread-slot underfill reduces latency hiding for arithmetic pipelines.
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[22]
        # Register allocation pressure limits concurrent latency-hiding CTAs.
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[13]
        # Shared-memory allocation pressure limits CTA residency and buffering.
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[26]
        # Parallel split-K reduction arithmetic adds compute work in this regime.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[32]
    # Multistage kernels form a distinct family; retain the family-level effect.
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * w[2]
    # Extra fill/drain exposure moderates that family preference when reduction is short.
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[15]
    if p.output_work_per_sm > 1.0e3:
        # With adequate output parallelism, partial-reduction traffic is not justified by scarce work.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[29]
        # Fixed thread coordination and issue work is exposed once dispatch is amortized.
        s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[30]
    else:
        # For small grids, retaining fewer waves reduces exposed launch and dispatch overhead.
        s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[1]
    # Resolve multistage depth by actual depth in small total-work problems.
    s = s + np.where(p.log_flops < 24.0, (f.stage_count - 2.0) / 14.0, 0.0) * w[24]
    s = s + np.where(p.log_flops < 24.0, ((f.stage_count - 2.0) / 14.0) * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction, 0.0) * w[11]
    s = s + np.where(p.log_flops < 24.0, ((f.stage_count - 2.0) / 14.0) * f.occupancy_deficit, 0.0) * w[25]
    s = s + np.where(p.log_flops < 24.0, ((f.stage_count - 2.0) / 14.0) * f.register_file_pressure, 0.0) * w[20]
    # For long-work problems, staging overhead is amortized, so retain a separate depth effect.
    s = s + np.where(p.log_flops >= 24.0, ((f.stage_count - 2.0) / 14.0) * (1.0 - f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction), 0.0) * w[3]
    # Scarce resident blocks amplify fixed per-CTA thread coordination overhead.
    s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[17]
    # CTA output area is a multiplicative scheduling-granularity cost; calibrate it separately
    # for memory/compute and low/high output-work regimes rather than folding it into edge waste.
    s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1.0, np.where(p.output_work_per_sm > 1.0e3, np.log2(f.absolute_output_tile_area), 0.0), 0.0) * w[23]
    s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1.0, np.where(p.output_work_per_sm <= 1.0e3, np.log2(f.absolute_output_tile_area), 0.0), 0.0) * w[14]
    s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio >= 1.0, np.where(p.output_work_per_sm > 1.0e3, np.log2(f.absolute_output_tile_area), 0.0), 0.0) * w[31]
    s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio >= 1.0, np.where(p.output_work_per_sm <= 1.0e3, np.log2(f.absolute_output_tile_area), 0.0), 0.0) * w[6]
    if p.log_flops >= 32.5 and p.output_work_per_sm < 234057:
        # split-K sweet spot: quadratic in log2(K-loop iterations per serial split), interior optimum
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count)) * w[10]
        s = s + np.square(np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count))) * w[12]
    if p.roofline_ratio >= 1 and p.output_work_per_sm > 200000:
        # large-grid branch (r09): CTA residency and register pressure on huge compute-bound grids

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # output-boundary overwork, compressed because edge waste spans hundreds
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[2]
    # final-wave idle time grows sharply as the usable wave fraction vanishes
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 / np.clip(1.0 - f.tail_waste, 1e-6, 1.0)) * w[7]
    # one-wave or otherwise poorly amortized grid dispatch overhead
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[27]
    # register spilling introduces a severe local-memory latency penalty
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[4]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[11]
    # tile geometry and insufficient internal work expose CTA overhead
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch) * w[3]
    s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[6]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch) * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[35]
    # pipeline prologue and epilogue overhead is poorly amortized by short reductions
    s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[32]
    # Short-grid shapes have less independent work to hide split-K reduction costs.
    if p.log_min_dim < 5:
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[9]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[8]
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[31]
        # A normalized dependency fraction becomes more costly as the absolute K loop grows.
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[20]
        # Elongated tiles can alter the scheduling cost of serial split-K dependencies.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch) * f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[30]
    else:
        # Longer reductions amortize some fixed effects, but retain partial-reduction costs.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[37]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[23]
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[17]
        # Long-loop accumulation still makes serial dependency costly in absolute terms.
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[24]
        # The geometry/dependency tradeoff has a distinct coefficient for long reductions.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch) * f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[10]
    # Memory-bound shapes are governed by replicated operand traffic and weak tile intensity.
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[28]
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[15]
        # Multistage designs have a distinct async-copy and buffering schedule.
        s = s + f.stage_family * w[12]
        # Integer CTA packing creates a distinct partially populated whole wave.
        s = s + f.cta_wave_quantization * w[33]
        # Large per-iteration staging bursts are most exposed when pipeline overhead
        # is poorly amortized, rather than being treated as aggregate K traffic.
        s = s + np.log2(f.k_tile_staging_bytes) * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[14]
    else:
        # Compute-bound shapes are governed by front-end work and CTA residency.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[21]
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[18]
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[5]
        s = s + f.stage_family * w[0]
        # Keep grid quantization separate from normalized final-wave idleness.
        s = s + f.cta_wave_quantization * w[16]
        # Well-supplied rectangular outputs need a balanced CTA geometry and
        # should price scheduling and resource pressure as one concurrency regime.
        balanced_rectangular = (p.output_work_per_sm > 1024.0 and
                                p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.25)
        s = s + np.where(balanced_rectangular,
                         f.warp_schedule_count / 1024.0, 0.0) * w[26]
        s = s + np.where(balanced_rectangular,
                         f.resident_block_scarcity, 0.0) * w[1]
        s = s + np.where(balanced_rectangular,
                         f.register_file_pressure, 0.0) * w[13]
        s = s + np.where(balanced_rectangular,
                         f.shared_memory_pressure, 0.0) * w[29]
        s = s + np.where(balanced_rectangular,
                         f.resident_block_scarcity *
                         (f.register_file_pressure + f.shared_memory_pressure), 0.0) * w[34]
        # The same staging-granularity effect remains relevant for compute-bound
        # kernels, but receives a separate fitted coefficient for that bottleneck.
        s = s + np.log2(f.k_tile_staging_bytes) * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[22]
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 249661 and p.roofline_ratio >= 1.32805:
        # split-K sweet spot: quadratic in log2(K-loop iterations per serial split), interior optimum
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count)) * w[19]
        s = s + np.square(np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count))) * w[36]

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Boundary overhang increases executed work; compress the wide edge-waste range.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[18]
    # A register spill introduces very expensive local-memory traffic.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[12]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[35]
    s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[15]

    # A moderate rectangular, dense shape gets its own geometry response without
    # multiplying the parent rule's reduction and roofline execution paths.
    geom = p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.35 or p.output_work_per_sm < 256
    moderate_rectangular_dense = (
        p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.35
        and p.output_aspect_imbalance < 0.75
        and p.output_work_per_sm >= 256
    )
    s = s + np.where(
        moderate_rectangular_dense,
        np.log2(1.0 + f.tail_waste / np.fmax(1e-3, 1.0 - f.tail_waste)),
        0.0,
    ) * w[5]
    s = s + np.where(moderate_rectangular_dense, f.wave_count_deficit, 0.0) * w[23]
    # Mismatch is allowed to be beneficial in this crossover regime.
    s = s + np.where(
        moderate_rectangular_dense,
        np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch),
        0.0,
    ) * w[3]
    # Preserve the parent preferences for sparse/rectangular and square-like shapes.
    s = s + np.where(
        moderate_rectangular_dense,
        0.0,
        np.where(
            geom,
            np.log2(1.0 + f.tail_waste / np.fmax(1e-3, 1.0 - f.tail_waste)),
            0.0,
        ),
    ) * w[25]
    s = s + np.where(moderate_rectangular_dense, 0.0, np.where(geom, f.wave_count_deficit, 0.0)) * w[37]
    s = s + np.where(
        moderate_rectangular_dense,
        0.0,
        np.where(geom, np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch), 0.0),
    ) * w[22]
    s = s + np.where(
        moderate_rectangular_dense,
        0.0,
        np.where(
            geom,
            0.0,
            np.log2(1.0 + f.tail_waste / np.fmax(1e-3, 1.0 - f.tail_waste)),
        ),
    ) * w[4]
    s = s + np.where(moderate_rectangular_dense, 0.0, np.where(geom, 0.0, f.wave_count_deficit)) * w[36]
    s = s + np.where(
        moderate_rectangular_dense,
        0.0,
        np.where(geom, 0.0, np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch)),
    ) * w[16]

    # In underfilled or low-absolute-work shapes, CTA thread overhead is poorly amortized.
    low_absolute_work = p.output_work_per_sm < 256 or p.log_flops < 20
    s = s + np.where(low_absolute_work, f.thread_work_granularity_deficit, 0.0) * w[14]
    s = s + f.oriented_tile_aspect_mismatch * w[8]
    # Penalize multistage buffering once shared memory approaches the per-block limit.
    sm_excess = np.fmax(0.0, (f.shared_memory_pressure - 0.75) / 0.25)
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * sm_excess * w[42]
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * sm_excess * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[2]
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * sm_excess * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[13]
    # Register pressure is penalized only after a high-pressure threshold is crossed.
    reg_excess = np.fmax(0.0, (f.register_file_pressure - 0.70) / 0.30)
    s = s + reg_excess * f.has_spill * np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[39]
    underfilled = p.output_work_per_sm < 256
    s = s + np.where(underfilled, reg_excess * f.wave_count_deficit, 0.0) * w[7]
    s = s + np.where(underfilled, 0.0, reg_excess * f.resident_block_scarcity) * w[28]
    s = s + reg_excess * f.resident_block_scarcity * f.has_spill * w[38]

    # Short-dimension/reduction-scale regimes expose different fixed pipeline costs.
    if p.log_min_dim < 6:
        s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[20]
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[30]
        s = s + f.k_tail_waste * w[9]
        s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * w[17]
        s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[33]
        if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
            s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[6]
            s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[32]
            s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[29]
            s = s + f.k_tail_waste * w[41]
        else:
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[43]
            s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[11]
            s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[24]
            s = s + f.k_tail_waste * w[34]
    else:
        s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[10]
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[0]
        s = s + f.k_tail_waste * w[40]
        s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * w[26]
        s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[27]
        if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
            s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[6]
            s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[32]
            s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[29]
            s = s + f.k_tail_waste * w[41]
        else:
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[43]
            s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[11]
            s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[24]
            s = s + f.k_tail_waste * w[34]
    if p.log_flops >= 32.5 and p.output_work_per_sm < 234057:
        # split-K sweet spot: quadratic in log2(K-loop iterations per serial split), interior optimum
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count)) * w[31]
        s = s + np.square(np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count))) * w[19]
    if p.roofline_ratio >= 1 and p.output_work_per_sm > 200000:
        # large-grid branch (r09): CTA residency and register pressure on huge compute-bound grids
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[21] + f.register_file_pressure * w[1]
    return s
